defects: Single unbroken 15 s take: the structure is one zoom-out, then a pattern shift, then a title card. There is no change of scale or angle after about 5 s.
Frame 1 is a lone tile on a flat grey-beige gradient. It reads as an unfinished empty stage, not a composed opening.
During the offset phase the rows overlap and clip each other. Circles are cut into half-arcs with grout lines running through them, so the clean tile logic turns into visual noise behind the title.
Between pairs the pattern moves almost uniformly sideways. There is no visible ease-in or ease-out and no overshoot, and the motion has no weight. It looks like a linear scroll on a background layer.
The title card is a flat cream rectangle composited on top of the pattern. It does not sit in the tile grid or take on its texture or light, so it reads as a pasted lower-third.
The final 4–5 s is a held title card over a looping pattern scroll. The change-per-second values plateau around 20 with no settle beat.

Audio: two near-identical noise risers at about 7.8 s and 9.0 s, then one broadband transient at about 10.1 s. The risers are copy-pasted, with the same shape and length. The pluck layer has static harmonics, with a few evenly spaced partials and no timbral development.

The 100% crop is clean, but the blue blotch texture is applied uniformly to every tile. It reads as one procedural noise overlay, not variation between individual glazed tiles. The grout has no depth or shadow.
gaps: Motion: the 'offset' concept, a tile shifted into a pattern, is good but only played once and literally. Top studios would vary the device (rotation, mirroring, colour inversion, rows sliding into place with mass and settle), stage a clear peak at about 70%, and land the title by having the tiles themselves form or reveal it. Here a card is placed on top.

Sound: generic pluck loop plus stock risers and one impact. There is no tile or ceramic Foley (clinks, slides, grout scrape) tied to on-screen events, no arrangement development after 4 s, and no clear sync between row shifts and transients. It needs a bespoke sound pass where each tile placement or offset has a material sound and the mix opens up at the reveal.

Finish and material: the azulejo surface is flat. Real glaze needs specular highlights, slight tile-to-tile tonal and edge irregularity, crackle, and grout depth with contact shadow. Light falloff should move with the camera. Without these the piece looks like a vector pattern with a noise multiply, and the closing frame does not rhyme with the opening single tile.
